newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Strike at Cambior Omai could hit output.
newsitem.headline: Strike at Cambior Omai could hit output.

text.p: A strike at Cambior's Omai Gold Mines in Guyana could affect operations as early as Thursday night if no solution is found to the conflict, a spokeswoman said.

"The strike is not affecting output, our mill is still in operation," the spokeswoman, Seeta Mohamed, said by telephone from the Guayanese capital, Georgetown. "But operations could start being affected later this evening or tomorrow."
She said over 200 workers went on strike on Tuesday evening, out of a total workforce of more than 900, in protest over disciplinary measures applied to a maintenance employee.
The spokeswoman said negotiations between union representatives and management started at around noon local time (1500 GMT).
Montreal-based Cambior Inc owns 65 percent of the open-pit mine, U.S. Golden Star Resources Ltd percent and the Guyanese government the rest.
Cambior has projected gold production at Omai to increase to 340,000 ounces this year, from 255,000 ounces in 1996.
Gold is Guyana's second foreign currency earner after sugar if one includes Omai gold mine, the largest foreign investment in the country.
